summary: Refreshes the AHE evidence-ledger variant with Humanize-derived guarded completion rules observed in the PEP615/646/680 max3 traces.
meaningful_difference: Compared with ahe-evidence-ledger-v1, this variant makes completion harder for high-risk work. It classifies ACs by requirement source, forces workers to build an implementation surface inventory before narrowing scope, blocks required deferrals, treats manual-only evidence as partial, requires compliance fixtures for parsers/formats, requires cross-surface equivalence for duplicate implementations, prevents spec-mentioned duplicate surfaces from being dismissed merely because the worker skipped them, requires grammar/compiler coverage across AST/runtime/future/negative syntax surfaces, detects stale summaries, and lets reviewers invalidate over-broad derived ACs instead of chasing scope drift.

predicted_case_effects.prediction: Reviewer should block completion until fixture-driven TOML compliance and error tests are present or explicitly proven non-applicable.

Worker should identify C accelerator, pure-Python fallback, metadata, import, cache, and runtime surfaces before scope narrowing; reviewer should require equivalence evidence for timezone transition parsing and related edge behavior.
Reviewer should require automated grammar/AST/future-annotations regressions while preventing over-broad derived ACs from expanding the original task.
